Configuration # Use a strong secret from environment; provide a fallback for local dev but ensure it's long APP_SECRET = os.getenv("APP_SECRET", "a_very_long_and_secure_random_fallback_secret_key_123456789") ALGORITHM = "HS256" ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES = 60 DB_PATH = "db.sqlite3" # Use parameterized-like schema creation conn.execute(""" CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, username TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL ) """) conn.execute(""" CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS secrets ( username TEXT PRIMARY KEY, secret_value TEXT NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY (username) REFERENCES users(username) ) """) conn.commit() init_db() # --- Models --- # Added constraints to prevent resource exhaustion (max lengths) class UserRegister(BaseModel): email: EmailStr username: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=100) password: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=128) class UserLogin(BaseModel): email: EmailStr password: str = Field(..., max_length=128) class SecretSet(BaseModel): username: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=100) secret: str = Field(..., max_length=10000) # Bound request size for the secret class TokenResponse(BaseModel): token: str message: str # --- Helpers --- def create_access_token(data: dict): to_encode = data.copy() expire = datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(minutes=ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES) to_encode.update({"exp": expire}) # jose.jwt.encode handles the signature and algorithm correctly return jwt.encode(to_encode, APP_SECRET, algorithm=ALGORITHM) async def get_current_user(auth: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials = Depends(security)): try: # Catch all JWT errors (expired, invalid signature, etc) and return 401 raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid authentication token") # --- Endpoints --- @app.post("/register", status_code=201) async def register(user: UserRegister, db: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db)): # Password hashing is handled by passlib (bcrypt) hashed_password = pwd_context.hash(user.password) try: # Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL Injection db.execute( "INSERT INTO users (email, username, password_hash) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (user.email, user.username, hashed_password) ) db.commit() except sqlite3.IntegrityError: # Parameterized query to prevent SQL Injection result = db.execute("SELECT password_hash, username FROM users WHERE email = ?", (user.email,)).fetchone() # Constant-time comparison is handled by passlib.verify if not result or not pwd_context.verify(user.password, result["password_hash"]): raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid email or password") token = create_access_token(data={"sub": result["username"]}) return {"token": token, "message": "Login successful"} @app.post("/set_secret") async def set_secret(data: SecretSet, current_user: str = Depends(get_current_user), db: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db)): #
